request.instruction:
You review a prior-authorization request against a medical policy's criteria.
For each criterion, decide from the evidence alone whether it is:
- "met": the evidence states that the criterion is satisfied,
- "not-met": the evidence states something that fails the criterion,
- "insufficient": the evidence does not say, or says it only vaguely, without a date, or as hearsay.
Cite every evidence reference you relied on, exactly as given (for example "DocumentReference/doc-1").
Never cite a reference that is not in the evidence list. Do not recommend an outcome.
Respond with JSON only:
{"findings": [{"criterionId": "...", "status": "met" | "not-met" | "insufficient", "evidence": ["..."], "rationale": "..."}]}

criteria.title: Obstructive sleep apnea is diagnosed
criteria.requirement: The member has a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea, recorded as a condition or stated by the prescriber.

criteria.title: Continuous pressure was tried and failed
criteria.requirement: The record documents a trial of at least 21 days of continuous positive airway pressure, and the prescriber states that it was not tolerated or did not control the apnea.

criteria.title: Apnea-hypopnea index of 18 or more
criteria.requirement: A sleep study dated within the 12 months before the request reports an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of at least 18 events per hour.

criteria.title: Bi-level settings were shown to work
criteria.requirement: A titration study or the prescriber's note documents that bi-level pressure at the ordered settings controlled the apnea.

evidence.text: Condition: J44.9 Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unspecified. Onset 2018-03-11.

Clinical note (Prescriber visit note, dated 2026-09-08T12:00:00Z):
His sleep study in March, done here on the eleventh, counted thirty-seven obstructive events
an hour, so obstructive sleep apnea on top of his lung disease.
He put in a solid three months on CPAP from April through June and hated every night of it;
he pulls the mask off within the hour and his machine still logs over twenty events an hour.
I do not think he can tolerate CPAP.
Last week we tried bi-level pressure in the lab: at 15 over 9 the events dropped to a couple
an hour and he slept through. I am ordering bi-level at those settings, no backup rate.

value.rationale: The prescriber states in the clinical note that the patient has a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea.
The record documents a trial of three months of CPAP from April through June, and the prescriber states that it was not tolerated and did not control the apnea.
The sleep study dated in March (within the 12 months before the request) reports thirty-seven obstructive events an hour, which is an AHI of at least 18 events per hour.
The prescriber's note documents that bi-level pressure at 15 over 9 controlled the apnea down to a couple of events an hour.
